title: Chlorpyrifos exposure induces inflammatory and immune dysregulation: An integrative in silico and in vitro analysis.
authors: Chiang, Chen-Yu; Chen, Shih-Pin; Luo, Ci-Wen; Su, Chun-Hung; Lee, Shiuan-Shinn; Chen, Wen-Ying; Chen, Chun-Jung; Tseng, Ching-Chi; Chen, Pin-Tzu; Lu, Yin-Che; Kuan, Yu-Hsiang
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过网络预测、分子对接和MD模拟探讨毒死蜱与MAPK14/RELA蛋白的相互作用及巨噬细胞炎症机制，对象为小分子-蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅方法部分可借鉴，与课题关联度低。
abstract: Chlorpyrifos (CPF) is a widely used organophosphate insecticide that has been associated with chronic inflammatory and immune-related health effects. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying CPF-induced immune-inflammatory dysregulation remain incompletely defined. In this study, an integrated in silico and in vitro strategy was employed to elucidate the signaling pathways involved in CPF-mediated macrophage inflammatory activation. Network-based target prediction and pathway enrichment analysis identified MAPK14, which encodes p38 MAPK, and RELA, which encodes the NF-kappaB p65 subunit, as central regulatory nodes potentially involved in CPF-mediated inflammatory responses. These computational findings guided subsequent mechanistic validation in RAW264.7 macrophages. Consistent with the in silico predictions, CPF exposure selectively increased the activation of MAPK14 (which encodes the p38 MAPK) and RELA (which represents p65) in RAW264.7 macrophages, whereas other MAPK family members showed no obvious activation. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations further demonstrated stable interactions between CPF and both predicted targets, supporting their potential involvement in CPF-responsive signaling regulation. Functionally, CPF treatment increased phosphorylation of p38 MAPK and p65, promoted the production of inflammatory mediators, and upregulated co-stimulatory and antigen-presenting molecules in macrophages. Collectively, these findings suggest that CPF is associated with macrophage-mediated inflammatory activation involving the p38 MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling pathways. This study provides mechanistic insight into CPF-associated immune-inflammatory dysregulation and supports the relevance of macrophage inflammatory activation in environmental CPF exposure.
abstract_zh: 毒死蜱（Chlorpyrifos, CPF）是一种广泛使用的有机磷杀虫剂，与慢性炎症和免疫相关健康效应有关。然而，CPF诱导的免疫-炎症失调的分子机制仍未完全阐明。本研究采用整合的计算机模拟（in silico）和体外（in vitro）策略，以阐明CPF介导的巨噬细胞炎症激活所涉及的信号通路。基于网络的靶点预测和通路富集分析确定了MAPK14（编码p38 MAPK）和RELA（编码NF-kappaB p65亚基）作为可能参与CPF介导炎症反应的核心调控节点。这些计算发现指导了后续在RAW264.7巨噬细胞中的机制验证。与计算机模拟预测一致，CPF暴露选择性增加了RAW264.7巨噬细胞中MAPK14（编码p38 MAPK）和RELA（代表p65）的激活，而其他MAPK家族成员未显示明显激活。分子对接和分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟进一步证明了CPF与两个预测靶点之间的稳定相互作用，支持其在CPF响应性信号调控中的潜在参与。在功能上，CPF处理增加了p38 MAPK和p65的磷酸化，促进了炎症介质的产生，并上调了巨噬细胞中的共刺激和抗原呈递分子。总体而言，这些发现表明CPF与涉及p38 MAPK和NF-kappaB信号通路的巨噬细胞介导的炎症激活相关。本研究为CPF相关的免疫-炎症失调提供了机制性见解，并支持巨噬细胞炎症激活在环境CPF暴露中的相关性。
